predecessors.name: Western Turkic Khaganate (Western Göktürks)
predecessors.text: Tokharistan, 'invaded' by Tong Yabgu in 625 and ruled by his son Tardush Shad

successors.name: Turk Shahis (Kabul Shahi)
successors.text: the Turk Shahis, 'a probable political extension and vassals of the neighbouring Yabghus'

successors.name: Tang dynasty
successors.text: Badakhshan, where the remnants survived until 758 and Wu-na-to visited the Chinese court

ledger.x: 625: Tong Yabgu invades Tokharistan and installs his son Tardush Shad at Kunduz.
657: the Western Turkic Khaganate falls and Tokharistan is the Yabghus' own.
718: the Chinese account of 718 lists Khuttal, Chaghanian, Kabul and Zabul under the Yabghu.

wars.name: Arab conquest of Tokharistan
wars.outcome: The Arabs under Abdallah ibn Amir conquered the whole of Tokharistan in 652-653; the Yabghus remained under Tang suzerainty.

wars.name: Qutayba's reconquest of Tokharistan
wars.outcome: 'In 710, Qutaiba ibn Muslim was able to re-establish Muslim control over Tokharistan'; the Yabghu was exiled to Damascus.

certainty.note: Tokharistan is described by valleys and mountain edges; the 659 Tang list and the 718 Chinese list are of states, not borders.

sources.title: Protectorate General to Pacify the West
